title: Integrated Budgeting, Contracts, Procurement, and Revenue Recognition Playbook (Q2 2027)
author: Maya Patel
content:
Summary

This playbook documents Redwood Inference's end-to-end finance and legal procedures for: budgeting and forecasting, contracts intake and review, procurement approvals and vendor onboarding, and revenue recognition and billing policy (ASC 606-aligned). It provides step-by-step procedures, approval thresholds, control checks, and templates/references for Q2 2027 and ongoing operations.

Purpose and scope

- Purpose: Provide a single source of truth for finance and legal processes that materially affect cash flow, legal risk, and financial statement presentation.
- Scope: Applies to all Redwood legal entities and covers: annual budgeting; quarterly forecasts; contract lifecycle (RFP — signature — storage); vendor procurement and P-card controls; billing, invoicing cadence, revenue recognition, and credit memos. Exceptions must be approved by Head of Finance and General Counsel.

Ownership and contacts

- Document owner: Finance (Maya Patel, Director, FP&A)
- Process owners:
  - Budgeting & Forecasting: FP&A (Elena Rodriguez)
  - Contracts Intake & Review: Legal (Samir Khan)
  - Procurement & Vendor Ops: Procurement Lead (Priya Nair)
  - Revenue Recognition & Billing: Accounting (Alex Chen)
- Escalation path: Process owner — Head of Finance — General Counsel — CFO

Budgeting and forecasting cadence

1. Annual Budgeting (Timeline)
   - June–July: Strategy & target setting (executive OKR alignment).
   - Aug–Oct: Department submissions via Budget template (see Appendix A).
   - Nov: Finance consolidation and leadership review.
   - Dec 15: Board-approved budget finalized (effective Jan 1).

2. Quarterly Forecasting
   - Cadence: Forecasts due on the 10th business day after quarter close.
   - Inputs: Actuals (GL), pipeline adjustments, committed contracted revenue, headcount changes, known one-time items.
   - Ownership: FP&A prepares consolidated forecast; department leads validate changes.

3. Forecast Controls and Assumptions
   - All forecast changes > $250k ARR must be supported by a rationale memo and owner sign-off.
   - Sales-committed ARR only included when signed contract executed or when Sales provides a written customer commitment (email + AE manager sign-off).

Contracts: intake, review, and signature authority

1. Contract intake (initial steps)
   - All contract requests must be submitted via the Contract Intake form (Confluence link in Appendix B) and include: business owner, counterparty name, expected term, estimated value, data handling classification, and any special terms requested.
   - Legal triage within 2 business days: Legal assigns intake priority: Standard, Non-standard, or High Risk.

2. Review timelines and SLAs
   - Standard templates (SaaS Master Agreement, Statement of Work, NDA) — Legal review target: 3 business days.
   - Non-standard or high-risk contracts — Legal review target: 7–14 business days depending on risk.

3. Signature authority and approval thresholds
   - Executive Approval Matrix:
     | Contract Value (ARR or Term) | Required Approvals |
     | --------------------------- | ------------------ |
     | <= $50k                    | Business owner + Legal standard template sign-off |
     | $50k–$250k                 | Business owner + Finance (revenue impact) + Legal |
     | $250k–$1M                  | Business owner + Head of Finance + Legal + VP Sponsor |
     | > $1M                      | CFO + GC + CEO notification (board notice if strategic) |
   - Contracts that include indemnity, data residency, or source code escrow require GC approval regardless of dollar value.

4. Contract redlines and negotiation
   - Legal documents redlines tracked in the contract management system (DocuSign/CLM). Negotiation owners must upload each negotiated version and document key risk items in the negotiation log.

Procurement and vendor onboarding

1. Procurement request & approval flow
   - Purchase requests (PR) > $10k must have three-line justification, budget code, and vendor selection justification.
   - Approval thresholds:
     - <= $2k: Manager approval (can use P-card)
     - $2k–$10k: Department head approval
     - $10k–$100k: Procurement lead + Finance approval
     - > $100k: Procurement lead + Head of Finance + Legal review (if contract required)

2. Vendor due diligence checklist

- Mandatory checks before onboarding a new vendor with access to customer data or production systems:
  - Signed vendor questionnaire and data processing addendum (DPA).
  - Security posture evidence (SOC 2 Type II or equivalent) OR formal security assessment completed.
  - Tax/identity verification and W-9/W-8 collection.
  - Sanctions screening (OFAC/EU) passed.

3. Purchasing documentation and recordkeeping

- All purchase orders, contracts, and invoices stored in the Procurement folder in the corporate document repository (link in Appendix C). Retention: 7 years for contracts and financial records unless longer retention required by law.

4. Emergency procurement (fast-track)

- For urgent purchases impacting production or security, procurement lead can approve up to $50k with post-facto documentation to Finance within 48 hours. Any emergency purchase > $50k requires Head of Finance approval.

Revenue recognition and billing policy (summary)

Policy statement: Redwood recognizes revenue in accordance with ASC 606 — when control of promised goods or services is transferred to the customer in an amount that reflects the consideration expected in exchange for those goods/services.

Key principles and application

- Identify the contract: Only executed contracts (signed or equivalent evidence of customer commitment) are recognized as revenue sources.
- Identify performance obligations: Common obligations include hosted API access, dedicated capacity reservations, and support services. Each obligation should be evaluated for separability.
- Determine transaction price: Includes variable consideration (usage, overage) estimated using the expected value or most likely amount method; constrained if significant reversal risk exists.
- Allocate price to obligations: Allocate based on standalone selling prices (SSP). Use price catalogs and historical behavior to establish SSP where available.
- Recognize when obligations are satisfied:
  - Subscription/hosted API access: Recognize ratably over the contract term.
  - Dedicated capacity (reserved): If customer pays for reserved capacity regardless of usage, recognize ratably over the reservation period unless there is a distinct deliverable schedule.
  - Professional services / one-time onboarding: Recognize upon completion of the service or milestone if criteria for control transfer met.

Billing cadence and invoicing standards

- Standard billing frequencies:
  - Monthly subscription usage: invoiced monthly in arrears, net 30 payment terms unless otherwise negotiated.
  - Annual prepay/commit: invoiced at contract inception; recognized monthly (ratable) unless performance obligations dictate otherwise.
  - Overages and variable usage: invoiced monthly in arrears with clear supporting usage reports.

- Invoice requirements (must include):
  - Customer name, billing address, Redwood legal entity, invoice number, invoice date, contract reference, period covered, line-item description with quantity and unit price, subtotal, taxes, payment instructions.

Credit memos, disputes and collections

1. Dispute intake and resolution
   - Customer disputes must be submitted to billing@redwoodinference.com and logged in the billing tracker within 24 hours of receipt.
   - Disputes investigated within 5 business days. Root cause analysis and remediation plan documented.

2. Credit memos
   - Credit memos issued for validated disputes or billing errors. Authorization levels for credit memos mirror contract approval thresholds. Credit memos > $10k require Head of Finance sign-off.

3. Collections policy
   - Late payment follow-up cadence: 7 days (reminder) — 30 days (collections notice) — 60 days (senior collections + legal referral) — 90 days (escalation to Head of Finance and possible contract suspension).

Accounting entries and example journal entries

- Example: Annual prepaid commitment (customer prepays $120,000 for 12 months of hosted API access)
  - On invoice receipt: Dr Cash $120,000 / Cr Deferred revenue (liability) $120,000
  - Monthly recognition (1/12): Dr Deferred revenue $10,000 / Cr Revenue $10,000

- Example: Monthly usage billing $15,000 invoiced in arrears
  - On month-end: Dr Accounts receivable $15,000 / Cr Revenue $15,000

Controls and auditability

- Required evidence for revenue recognition: executed contract, invoice, usage report, and policy mapping to performance obligations.
- Monthly revenue close checklist: revenue trigger report reconciliation, deferred revenue roll-forward, contract changes log review, journal entry approvals.
- Internal and external audit: maintain working papers and reconciliations; provide SOC/financial evidence on request.

Exceptions and escalation

- Any deviation from this playbook (e.g., non-standard billing terms, unusual revenue deferral) requires documented exception request and approval by Head of Finance and GC.
